# Workload Placement and Hardware Fabrics\chaptersubtitle{Partitioning Compute across Cloud, Host, Accelerator, and MCU}

![Systems Organ Focus: Whole-System Heterogeneous Silicon Placement across Cloud, Host MPU, Neural Accelerator NPU, and Real-Time MCU.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch09 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an autonomous robot that runs flawlessly on the test bench suffer violent latency spikes when deployed inside a sealed chassis?*

In cloud software architecture, computation is treated as an abstract, fungible commodity: microservices are deployed into elastic clusters where physical silicon placement is hidden behind virtualization layers. In Physical AI, silicon topology is a non-negotiable physical boundary. Moving bits across off-chip memory buses consumes orders of magnitude more energy than arithmetic, shared memory crossbars choke when camera DMA bursts contend with neural weight streaming, and unmanaged thermal dissipation triggers hardware downclocking that blows past real-time stopping deadlines. Designing an embodied system requires deliberate workload placement—mapping cognitive stages across cloud servers, Linux host processors, neural accelerators, and real-time microcontrollers based on cadence, memory bandwidth, and physical trust boundaries.

{{< pagebreak >}}

By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Map Pipeline Stages to Heterogeneous Silicon:** Partition the 7 canonical agent organs across Cloud, Linux Host (MPU), Neural Accelerator (NPU), and Real-Time Microcontroller (MCU) fabrics based on execution cadence, memory bandwidth, and trust boundaries.
2. **Budget Heterogeneous Hardware Resources:** Construct whole-system resource ledgers balancing arithmetic intensity ($\text{FLOPs}/\text{Byte}$), static SRAM footprints, LPDDR5 bus throughput, and thermal design power (TDP).
3. **Mitigate Interconnect Contention:** Architect Quality-of-Service (QoS) bus arbitration schemes that guarantee microsecond preemption for 1 kHz safety packets over high-bandwidth video DMA bursts.
4. **Enforce Deterministic Shared-Memory IPC:** Implement lock-free, zero-allocation circular ring buffers across non-coherent memory domains using atomic sequence counters and explicit cache maintenance operations.
5. **Evaluate Re-Placement Ripple Effects:** Quantify how relocating neural models across compute boundaries alters tail latency ($P_{99}$), thermal throttling margins ($T_j$), battery endurance, and physical stopping envelopes ($d_{\text{stop}}$).
6. **Freeze the Placement Ledger (PLACE-01):** Construct the ninth artifact of the engineering notebook establishing whole-system hardware allocations, interconnect priorities, and fallback triggers.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Compute in Physical AI is not an abstract cloud commodity; embodied architectures must deliberately partition algorithms across silicon fabrics based on execution cadence, memory bus bandwidth, thermal dissipation, and safety isolation.

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Insulated Cold-Vault Collision"}
**Platform:** 1.2-ton Autonomous Heavy Pallet Mover ($v = 1.8\text{ m/s}$).
**Failure Mechanism:** To save onboard compute costs, the VLA policy was offloaded to an edge 5G server; entering a cold-storage vault created an RF multipath blackout of $1,420\text{ ms}$.
**Root Cause:** Drive torque commands remained latched during the wireless dropout without local fallback trajectory caches or an independent MCU stopping supervisor.
**Physical Consequence:** The vehicle coasted unguided for $2.56\text{ m}$ ($+1.36\text{ m}$ past obstacle clearance), smashing into a steel building pillar at $1.8\text{ m/s}$ ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ damage).
:::


## The Monolithic Illusion vs. Physical Silicon

In modern cloud software engineering, computation is treated as an abstract, fungible commodity. You write Python, compile containers, and deploy microservices into a serverless cluster. Where a function physically executes—whether on CPU core 3, an adjacent server rack, or an elastic cloud datacenter three states away—is intentionally hidden behind virtualization layers. If a database query blocks or network latency spikes, client threads wait, HTTP retries absorb transient packet drops, and garbage collectors quietly sweep heap memory.

In Physical AI Systems, the topology of silicon is an inescapable physical boundary. The moment software moves physical matter—accelerating a multi-kilogram robotic arm, steering an autonomous rover across rough terrain, or actuating high-pressure surgical tools—where an algorithm runs dictates whether the machine survives. A machine learning policy boasting $99.9\%$ semantic grasping accuracy is useless if its weight fetches are stalled by an unthrottled camera DMA burst, causing an inverter control loop to miss its hard real-time deadline.

Every physical agent is governed by three fundamental silicon constraints: the physics of data movement (fetching bytes from DRAM consumes $200\times$ more energy than computing on them); the shared interconnect bottleneck (UMA crossbars saturating under concurrent DMA and tensor weight streams); and the thermodynamic derating cliff (DVFS downclocking under sustained junction heating).

Workload placement is not an arbitrary systems design preference. It is a rigorous mathematical mapping of cognitive workloads onto silicon substrates governed by latency, bandwidth, energy, and physical trust boundaries. We now examine how embodied workloads partition across the four tiers of compute.


## Algorithmic Workload Partitioning across Compute Tiers

Embodied intelligence spans four orders of magnitude in execution cadence ($0.1\text{ Hz} \to 1000\text{ Hz}$). Mapping these stages to silicon yields a four-tier compute hierarchy (@tbl-compute-tiers):

| Compute Fabric Tier | Hardware Substrate | Primary Architectural Role | Typical Execution Cadence | Memory Architecture | Physical Trust Level |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 4: Cloud / Fleet** | Multi-GPU Datacenter Cluster | Fleet learning, large foundational training, global route optimization | $0.001\text{--}0.1\text{ Hz}$ | Terabytes HBM3 / Non-Volatile Storage | **Untrusted:** Non-deterministic WAN latency |
| **Tier 3: Host Processor (MPU)** | 64-bit Multi-Core ARM Cortex-A | Semantic reasoning (VLMs), spatial frame graphs (`tf2`), Linux user-space daemons | $0.5\text{--}10\text{ Hz}$ | 4–16 GB LPDDR5 Unified Memory (UMA) | **Untrusted:** Non-real-time OS jitter ($P_{99} > 100\text{ ms}$) |
| **Tier 2: Neural Accelerator (NPU)** | Systolic Array / Edge GPU | Spatial affordance tokenization (DINOv2), multi-step Action Chunking (ACT, Diffusion) | $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ | On-Chip SRAM Tiling + DRAM DMA | **Untrusted Proposal Service:** High-throughput tensor compute |
| **Tier 1: Real-Time Controller (MCU)** | 32-bit Bare-Metal Cortex-M4 / RISC-V | 1 kHz Control Barrier Functions, dynamic stopping enforcement, PWM motor inverters | **$1000\text{ Hz} \pm 5\,\mu\text{s}$** | 256 KB Zero-Wait-State Internal SRAM | **Fully Trusted Authority:** Sole hardware access to gate drivers |

: Four-Tier Heterogeneous Silicon Placement Hierarchy. Systematic allocation of cognitive organs across compute fabrics based on cadence, memory, and safety privilege. {#tbl-compute-tiers}

By mapping System 2 deliberation to Tier 3, System 1.5 trajectory chunking to Tier 2, and System 1 reflexes to Tier 1, the system decouples high-bandwidth neural weight loading from microsecond motor deadlines.


## Silicon Interconnects, Memory QoS, and IPC Fabrics

Heterogeneous System-on-Chips share on-die interconnect fabrics. Unmanaged traffic creates crossbar saturation that stalls real-time execution.

### Memory Interconnect Bandwidth and Quality of Service (QoS)

On an embedded SoC with a Unified Memory Architecture (UMA), memory masters compete for crossbar access. Without bus arbitration, high-bandwidth camera DMA writes ($>1.5\text{ GB/s}$) collide with NPU tensor weight streaming ($20\text{ GB/s}$ bursts).

Physical AI systems enforce hardware AXI Quality of Service (QoS) priorities:

1. **Real-Time MCU SRAM Reads (`QoS = 15`):** Absolute highest priority.
2. **NPU Model Weight Fetches (`QoS = 10`):** Second priority.
3. **Camera Sensor DMA Writes (`QoS = 4`):** Throttled into FIFO buffers during bus contention.

### Lock-Free Shared SRAM Ring Buffers

To communicate across the Linux MPU and real-time MCU boundary without non-deterministic locking primitives, inter-processor communication (IPC) uses lock-free circular ring buffers in statically allocated internal SRAM:

```c
// LOCK-FREE INTER-PROCESSOR COMMUNICATION BUFFER (Shared SRAM)
typedef struct {
    uint32_t head_sequence;            // Written by producer (MPU)
    uint32_t tail_sequence;            // Read by consumer (MCU)
    uint32_t buffer_capacity;
    uint32_t payload_size_bytes;
    uint8_t  data_arena[SRAM_BUFFER_SIZE];
} lockless_sram_ring_t;
```


## Physical Dynamics, Thermal Headroom & The Cold-Vault Autopsy Deep-Dive

Moving computation to silicon exposes physical limits in energy, heat, and communication:

### The Energy Cost of Data Movement

Arithmetic is cheap; data transport is expensive. In 7 nm silicon, an 8-bit integer MAC consumes $0.2\text{ pJ}$, while an LPDDR5 DRAM access burns $150\text{ pJ}$ ($750\times$ ratio). Pushing neural layers to on-chip SRAM tiling maximizes arithmetic intensity ($\text{FLOPs/Byte}$) and preserves battery runtime.

### Dynamic Thermal Throttling (DVFS)

Sustained high-load neural inference dissipates heat:

$$C_{\text{die}} \frac{d T_j}{dt} = P_{\text{dynamic}} + P_{\text{leakage}} - \frac{T_j - T_{\text{ambient}}}{R_{\theta}}$$

When junction temperature $T_j > 85^\circ\text{C}$, Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) cuts accelerator clock rates by up to $60\%$, doubling inference latency and breaching intent validity leases.

### Detailed Autopsy Breakdown: The Insulated Cold-Vault Collision

![The Autonomous Heavy Pallet Mover Platform. Offloading policy execution to a 5G edge server caused a fatal crash when entering a cold-storage vault that blocked RF signals for $1,420\text{ ms}$.](figures/fig09_agv_mover_cropped.jpg){#fig-agv-mover width=100%}

In the autopsy introduced in the prologue, a 1.2-ton pallet mover traveling at $v = 1.8\text{ m/s}$ had its policy offloaded to a 5G server. Entering a cold vault created an RF multipath dropout of $1,420\text{ ms}$. During this window, the unguided vehicle coasted:

$$d_{\text{react}} = 1.8\text{ m/s} \times 1.42\text{ s} = 2.56\text{ meters}$$

With clearance to a steel building pillar of $d_{\text{clearance}} = 1.20\text{ m}$, the overrun of $+1.36\text{ m}$ smashed the vehicle into the pillar at full speed ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ replacement).

| Timestamp | Subsystem & Substrate | Recorded State / Telemetry Event | Physical Implication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$T + 84.210\text{ s}$** | 5G RF Transceiver (Vehicle) | Vehicle crosses cold-storage vault threshold; steel-clad insulation panel blocks 5G signals. | RF signal-to-noise ratio drops to zero. |
| **$T + 84.250\text{ s}$** | Linux Host MPU (Vehicle) | TCP socket enters retransmit timeout; high-level VLA trajectory stream halts. | $1,420\text{ ms}$ communication blackout begins. |
| **$T + 84.500\text{ s}$** | Inverter PWM Controller | Lacking local trajectory cache or MCU watchdog, inverter latches last forward drive torque ($240\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$). | 1.2-ton machine coasts unguided at $1.8\text{ m/s}$. |
| **$T + 85.000\text{ s}$** | Vehicle Chassis / Front Linkage | Vehicle traverses $1.42\text{ m}$, completely exhausting physical clearance ($d_{\text{clearance}} = 1.20\text{ m}$). | Collision unavoidable; zero braking engaged. |
| **$T + 85.630\text{ s}$** | Chassis / Steel Building Pillar | Vehicle strikes steel pillar at $1.8\text{ m/s}$ ($E_k = 1{,}944\text{ J}$). | Steering linkage shears; hydraulic lines rupture ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ damage). |
| **Root Cause** | *Systems Bottleneck* | Offloading real-time policy authority across an unbudgeted, stochastic wireless network without local trajectory fail-safes. |
| **Architectural Flaw** | *Privilege & Co-Design* | Lack of local MCU heartbeat watchdog and absence of onboard autonomous stopping distance supervisor ($d_{\text{stop}}$). |

## The Placement Specification and Systems Contract

To establish a formal hardware mapping across compute fabrics, the systems architecture defines the **Workload Placement Specification (PLACE-01)** (@tbl-dossier-place-01):

| Subsystem Domain | Architectural Parameter | Guaranteed Invariant & Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 1 (MCU) Execution** | `core_type`<br>`clock_hz`<br>`sram_bytes` | ARM Cortex-M4 / RISC-V<br>$168.0\text{ MHz} \pm 10\text{ ppm}$<br>$256\text{ KB}$ (Zero Heap / Static Arrays Only) |
| **Tier 2 (NPU) Placement** | `model_type`<br>`target_cadence`<br>`sram_tiling_mb` | Diffusion Policy / ACT ($H=16$)<br>$20.0\text{ Hz}$ ($50\text{ ms}$ budget)<br>$\ge 8.0\text{ MB}$ dedicated weight SRAM |
| **Tier 3 (MPU) Placement** | `os_kernel`<br>`max_p99_latency_ms`<br>`dram_alloc_gb` | Linux 6.6 with `PREEMPT_RT`<br>$\le 35.0\text{ ms}$ nominal ($P_{99}$)<br>$4.0\text{ GB}$ LPDDR5 pinned memory |
| **Bus QoS Configuration** | `mcu_read_qos`<br>`npu_fetch_qos`<br>`dma_stream_qos` | `QoS = 15` (Highest priority)<br>`QoS = 10` (Medium-high priority)<br>`QoS = 4` (Throttled background priority) |
| **Thermal Envelopes** | `t_junction_max`<br>`fan_trip_temp`<br>`dvfs_derate_temp` | $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ maximum junction threshold<br>$65.0^\circ\text{C}$ active cooling trigger<br>$75.0^\circ\text{C}$ linear cadence scaling |

: The Workload Placement Specification (PLACE-01). Quantitative silicon parameters, bus QoS priorities, and thermal boundaries bridging Architecture to Integration. {#tbl-dossier-place-01}

### The Placement Co-Design Checkpoint Ledger

We conclude the Workload Placement stage by auditing its resolution across all foundational physical constraints (@tbl-placement-matrix-checkpoint):

| Physical Constraint | Placement Systems Tension | Chapter 9 Architectural Resolution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Time & Freshness** | Network and OS latency tails ($>1\text{ s}$) create blind execution. | **Strict Local Placement:** System 1 reflexes reside strictly on onboard MCU. |
| **Inertia & Stopping** | Large kinetic momentum requires guaranteed local stopping autonomy. | **Hardware Watchdog Timers ($15\text{ ms}$)** triggering local Category 1 braking. |
| **Actuation & Jerk** | Discrete IPC messages command jagged motor step changes. | **MCU Quintic Spline Interpolation** executed in zero-wait-state SRAM. |
| **Energy & Thermal** | Excessive DRAM accesses and NPU heating cause thermal throttling. | **On-Chip SRAM Model Tiling** and dynamic thermal derating ledgers. |
| **Silicon Determinism** | Shared UMA memory crossbar contention stalls critical threads. | **Hardware AXI QoS Priority Arbitration** (`ARQOS`/`AWQOS`). |

: Placement Co-Design Checkpoint Ledger. Systematic architectural accounting of workload placement across physical constraints. {#tbl-placement-matrix-checkpoint}

### Systems Fallacies in Workload Placement

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Wireless 5G Networks Are Fast Enough for Real-Time Safety"}
* **The Fallacy:** Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) in 5G networks provides sub-millisecond guarantees sufficient for closing real-time motor control loops.
* **The Physical Reality:** Wireless signals are subject to physical RF physics: multipath cancellation, Faraday shielding, antenna orientation nulls, and base station handovers. A 1-second radio dropout traveling at $2\text{ m/s}$ creates $2\text{ meters}$ of unguided kinetic travel. Real-time safety must execute on local, physically connected silicon.
:::

::: {.callout-fallacy title="Unified Memory Eliminates Data Transfer Bottlenecks"}
* **The Fallacy:** Sharing a single pool of LPDDR5 DRAM across CPU, GPU, and NPU eliminates all memory copying and communication bottlenecks.
* **The Physical Reality:** While UMA eliminates physical PCIe transfers, it creates intense memory crossbar contention. Camera DMA write bursts collide with NPU tensor weight fetches, inflating $P_{99}$ latency tails by over $300\%$ unless managed via hardware QoS priority arbitration [@hennessy2019computer].
:::


## Chapter Summary and Handoff to Chapter 10

This chapter established how cognitive workloads are deliberately placed across heterogeneous silicon fabrics. Physical AI rejects the cloud illusion of fungible compute, mapping multi-rate cognitive stages across Cloud, Host MPU, Neural Accelerator NPU, and Real-Time MCU based on cadence, memory bandwidth, and physical trust boundaries.

By enforcing hardware AXI QoS bus priorities, lock-free shared SRAM ring buffers, and local microcontroller fail-safes, we eliminate memory crossbar contention and guarantee that network dropouts never cause physical collisions.

In the following chapter, **Chapter 10 (Human-Machine Governance and Supervisory Authority)**, we explore how physical agents interact with human operators, establish transparent trust metrics, and govern the handoff of operational authority in safety-critical shared workspaces.
